acceptance_criteria: The spec passes consistently in a full-suite run, without retries, across repeated runs.
description:
e2e/lazy-deps.spec.js:104, 'markdown preview refuses to emit HTML without a sanitiser', intermittently sees an empty .note-markdown-preview instead of the escaped source.

Observed once in a full 106-spec run, then passed on an identical re-run of the same suite, and passes 3/3 in isolation on both main and a feature branch. So it is ordering or timing dependent, not a code defect.

Likely mechanism: the spec aborts the purify.min.js route and then clicks the text-only toggle. setupTextOnlyToggle overwrites paneData.content from noteEditors.get(id).monacoEditor.getValue() before rendering the preview, so whether Monaco has finished loading at that moment changes what gets rendered. Under full-suite load Monaco resolves at a different point than it does in isolation.

Worth fixing at the spec level by waiting for the editor to be ready before toggling, rather than by adding a retry -- a test that passes on the second attempt is how a suite stops being trusted.
title: Flaky e2e: markdown preview sanitiser spec fails only in a full-suite run

acceptance_criteria: A user can upload one or more files from the browser into the directory a folder pane is browsing, on both local and relay deployments, without SFTP. Files larger than the 1MB payload cap work. A collision prompts rather than silently overwriting. An interrupted or cancelled upload leaves no partial file behind.
description:
GitHub issue #30 (dgking80): uploading files currently requires SFTP-ing into the machine separately. Add upload through the app itself.

The binding constraint is transport. cloud/src/ws/relay.js:101 caps both relay sockets at maxPayload = 1MB, deliberately, to prevent memory exhaustion. Base64 inflates by a third, so a single-message upload tops out near 700KB -- not a credible SFTP replacement. Uploads therefore have to be chunked rather than sent whole, and raising the cap was rejected because it applies to every message type on both sockets.

Other constraints found while scoping:
- agentRequest is JSON over WebSocket with a 15s timeout, which is fine per chunk and not for a whole file.
- Local mode falls back to fetch() against the cloud, where express.json({ limit: '16kb' }) applies -- smaller than any sensible chunk, so that route needs its own limit.
- The agent dials out to the cloud and has no inbound HTTP, so a separate direct-upload channel is not available without an architecture change.
- validateWorkingDirectory already confines paths to $HOME or /tmp, which is the right boundary to reuse.

Agreed shape: chunked begin/chunk/commit over the existing WebSocket, writing to a temp file and atomically renaming on commit; prompt on collision offering overwrite or keep-both; folder pane toolbar button plus drag-and-drop onto the pane, with progress and cancel.
title: File upload to the files feature

acceptance_criteria: A multi-chunk upload writes the correct bytes to the destination. An out-of-order or unknown chunk id is rejected. A cancelled or abandoned upload leaves no file at the destination and no temp file behind. Paths outside $HOME and /tmp are refused. Unit tested.
close_reason: Done and merged in PR #60. agent/services/uploads.js implements begin/chunk/commit/abort: 512KB of file per chunk, streamed to a hidden temp file beside the destination and renamed in atomically on commit, so the destination path only ever holds a complete file. Sequence numbers are checked rather than trusted, since appends at a wrong offset produce a file of the right length that is silently wrong. Abandoned uploads are swept after five idle minutes. Covered by 29 unit tests including the interrupted, cancelled, overrun and traversal cases.
description:
Three endpoints in agent/src/messageRouter.js alongside the existing /api/files/* handlers:

POST /api/files/upload/begin  -> { path, size, overwrite } returns an upload id, after validateWorkingDirectory on the destination and a collision check. Opens a temp file beside the destination.
POST /api/files/upload/chunk  -> { id, seq, data } appends one base64 chunk. Rejects an out-of-order seq rather than writing at the wrong offset.
POST /api/files/upload/commit -> { id } fsyncs, closes, and renames the temp file into place. Atomic, so a dropped connection never leaves a half-written file at the destination.
DELETE /api/files/upload/:id  -> cancels and unlinks the temp file.

Chunks are sized so a base64 message stays under the 1MB relay cap: 512KB of file per chunk leaves ample headroom after the ~33% inflation plus JSON framing.

Needs a total size ceiling and an idle-timeout sweep so an abandoned upload cannot leave temp files accumulating in the user's home directory.
title: Agent-side chunked upload protocol

acceptance_criteria: Uploading via the button and via drag-and-drop both land files in the directory the pane is browsing, on local and relay deployments. Progress advances and cancel stops the upload. A collision prompts. Dropping an image on the canvas still creates a note. Covered by e2e.
close_reason:
Done and merged in PR #60. Toolbar button plus drag-and-drop on the folder pane, with per-file progress and cancel. The chunk size comes from the agent's begin response rather than being a constant on both sides. Drag handling counts nesting rather than tracking a boolean, because dragenter fires again for every child element crossed. Drops are claimed with stopPropagation so a folder-pane drop does not fall through to the canvas image-to-note path.

Note the correction recorded earlier: there was no cloud-side body limit to raise. The cloud implements no /api/files/* routes at all, so file operations always go through a connected agent, including in local hosting.
description:
A toolbar button beside New File and New Folder (pane-renderers.js:706) opening a native multi-file picker, plus drag-and-drop onto the folder pane with a drop-target overlay.

Care needed on the drop handler: dropping files on the canvas today creates an image note (menus.js:552), so the folder-pane drop must claim the event without breaking that path.

Client splits each file with File.slice into 512KB chunks and drives begin/chunk/commit, showing per-file progress from the chunk count and offering cancel, which aborts the remaining chunks and calls the cancel endpoint. On a name collision, prompt with overwrite or keep-both (auto-suffixed).

Local mode note: the fetch fallback hits express.json({ limit: '16kb' }) in cloud/src/index.js, so the upload route needs its own larger limit for that path.
notes: Correction to the description: the note about express.json({ limit: '16kb' }) blocking a local-mode fetch fallback is wrong. The cloud implements no /api/files/* routes at all -- cloud/src/routes/ has analytics, api, download, layouts, notifications and preferences only. File operations therefore always go through a connected agent, including in local hosting, where the agent connects over WebSocket to the local cloud. There is no cloud-side upload route to raise a body limit on.
title: Upload UI in the folder pane

acceptance_criteria: An oversized image is rejected with a clear message to the user, or chunked, and never closes the relay connection. A size guard exists on every path that turns a file into a data URL for an agentRequest.
close_reason:
Done and merged in PR #60. The guard lives in ws-transport rather than at the call sites, so no future feature can forget it: agentRequest rejects, sendWs refuses and logs. The budget is the whole images array rather than each image, because saving a note sends all of them in one request — three 400KB images breach a cap none of them approaches alone.

Two corrections to this issue as filed. The note-editor paste handler it names was dead code, removed in bd_49Agents-7b2.7; the live path is the canvas one in modules/menus.js, which is what the e2e drives. And the HTTP path has a separate 16kb limit that this does not address, filed as bd_49Agents-7b2.6.
description:
Pasting or dropping an image into a note reads it with FileReader.readAsDataURL and passes the result straight to agentRequest (src-client/modules/editors.js:93 and :596, src-client/modules/menus.js:552). There is no size check anywhere on that path.

cloud/src/ws/relay.js:101 caps both relay sockets at maxPayload = 1MB. A data URL is base64, so roughly a third larger than the file. Any image much over ~700KB -- an ordinary phone photo or a full-screen screenshot -- exceeds the cap, and the receiving WebSocket closes the connection rather than failing just that request. So pasting a large screenshot into a note drops the relay.

Found while scoping upload (gh-30), which hits the same cap deliberately and solves it by chunking.
title: Image paste with no size guard exceeds the relay cap and drops the connection

acceptance_criteria: Opening a file larger than the payload cap either streams it in chunks or fails with a clear message. It never closes the relay connection.
close_reason:
Done and merged in PR #60. The severity was worse than filed: the oversized message is the agent's response, so it overran the cap on the agent's own socket and the cloud closes a socket that overruns it. Opening a log file took the agent offline and every pane with it.

Deliberately not streamed. Saving a file pane sends its whole content in one request, so a streamed read would let someone open a file they could never save. A symmetric limit instead, with a test asserting the two ceilings stay in step. The check is on the JSON encoding rather than the file size on disk, since escaping and multi-byte characters both inflate it, with a stat first so a huge file is declined without being read into memory. EFBIG maps to 413.
description:
GET /api/files/read (agent/src/messageRouter.js:336) does readFileSync on the whole file and returns the content in a single JSON response, with no size check. Against the 1MB maxPayload in cloud/src/ws/relay.js:101, any file over roughly 1MB cannot be opened in a file pane at all, and the failure mode is the socket closing rather than a useful error.

The read side of the same limitation the upload work solves for writes. Deliberately scoped out of the upload epic's transport work, which was kept to the write path, but it wants the same chunking treatment -- or at minimum a size check that fails with a clear message instead of taking the connection down.
title: Files larger than the relay cap cannot be opened

acceptance_criteria: validateWorkingDirectory resolves before checking, so a traversal path starting inside a permitted root is refused by the function itself rather than by its callers. Existing callers that already resolve keep working. Covered by unit tests including the /tmp/../etc and $HOME/../.. cases. A decision is recorded on whether /private/tmp and os.tmpdir() should be permitted.
close_reason:
Done and merged in PR #60. Confirmed the hole first: '/tmp/../etc/shadow' and '$HOME/../../etc/passwd' both passed the old prefix match, and createTerminal and resumeTerminal pass a client-supplied working directory straight through to tmux as the session's directory.

Now expands only a leading tilde (the old unanchored replace spliced home into the middle of a name like back~ups), refuses relative paths rather than resolving them against the agent's own cwd, normalises, follows symlinks so a link out of a permitted root is refused, and matches each root under its canonical name too. Per the decision recorded on this issue: realpaths accepted, os.tmpdir() not added, symlinks followed. The return value is now canonical, so on macOS /tmp/x comes back as /private/tmp/x.
description:
agent/services/sanitize.js:35 checks the path it is handed by string prefix, after expanding a leading ~ but without normalising the result. So a path that starts inside a permitted root and then climbs out passes the check. Verified directly:

  validateWorkingDirectory('/tmp/../etc/shadow')        -> allowed, returns '/tmp/../etc/shadow'
  validateWorkingDirectory('$HOME/../../etc/passwd')    -> allowed

Every current caller in the message router happens to be safe, because expandAndValidatePath (messageRouter.js:73) calls resolve() before validating. The function's own contract does not say that, so any service calling it directly inherits a traversal hole. That is what the upload work hit: services/uploads.js now resolves before validating, in its own expandAndValidate helper, but the underlying sharp edge remains for the next caller.

Also worth noting while in there: the permitted roots are $HOME and the literal '/tmp'. On macOS /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp and os.tmpdir() returns /var/folders/..., so a caller reaching for the platform temp directory is refused, and a realpath'd /tmp path would be too. Whether that is intended is worth deciding rather than leaving to chance.

Found while building gh-30 upload.
title: validateWorkingDirectory accepts unresolved traversal paths

acceptance_criteria: A note with images either syncs them to cloud storage successfully, or does not attempt to and says so. No silent 413. A decision is recorded on whether cloud storage should hold image data at all.
description:
cloudSaveNote (src-client/modules/cloud.js:204) PUTs the whole images array to /api/cloud-notes/:id over HTTP. cloud/src/index.js:125 applies express.json({ limit: '16kb' }) globally, with no route override, and a data URL for any real image is comfortably past that.

Measured against the running server:
  10kb image -> 200
  20kb image -> 413
  300kb image -> 413

So note images above roughly 16kb have never synced to cloud storage. It fails silently: the client catches and logs '[Cloud] Note sync failed'. Notes sync their text across devices and lose their images.

Separate from the relay cap (bd_49Agents-7b2.3): that one is the WebSocket path to the agent, this is the HTTP path to cloud storage, and they have different limits and different failure modes.

The fix is a product decision rather than a technical one, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: either raise the body limit for this route and accept storing base64 images in the cloud database, or stop sending images on this path and accept that cloud-synced notes do not carry them. Worth deciding deliberately.
title: Note images never reach cloud storage: 16kb body limit returns 413

acceptance_criteria: Either the function is wired up and its .note-editor element rendered, or it and its unused import are removed and APP_MAP.md updated. No exported function remains that would throw on its first line if called.

Fixed; PR #61 is open and awaiting review. 154 deletions for 11 insertions.

setupNoteEditorListeners was imported by app.js and never called, and .note-editor has not been rendered since notes moved to Monaco, so it would have thrown on its second line. Its image paste handler is the first thing you find when investigating a note paste bug and is not the live path — I added a size guard to it during bd_49Agents-7b2.3 before noticing it was unreachable, which is how this surfaced. The three surviving .note-editor lookups in live code went with it, along with APP_MAP.md's entry.

Two of those dead branches were masking a real bug, filed as bd_49Agents-7b2.8: a note pane never takes editor focus.
description:
src-client/modules/editors.js:28 exports setupNoteEditorListeners, which app.js:29 imports and never calls. The element it hangs everything off, .note-editor, is never rendered either -- note panes render .note-editor-mount for Monaco and .note-markdown-preview. Were it ever invoked it would throw immediately on editor.addEventListener with editor null.

It is also actively misleading: the image paste handler in it looks like the live path for pasting an image into a note and is the first thing you find when investigating that. title: Dead code: setupNoteEditorListeners is never called

acceptance_criteria: Focusing a note pane, by click and by keyboard pane jump, puts the cursor in its editor so typing works immediately. Tab chords still function while a note is focused.
description:
Focusing a note pane does not focus anything you can type into. Two paths tried to, and both reached for a .note-editor textarea that notes have not rendered since they moved to Monaco (.note-editor-mount), so the branch was guarded by if (noteEditor) and never ran:

- pane-interaction.js, the pane focus handler, which also tried to place the cursor at the end of the text.
- shortcuts.js, the keyboard pane-jump handler, whose entire 'note' branch did nothing.

Both are dead branches rather than failures, so the symptom is silent: jump to a note with a pane number and you can look at it but not type into it without clicking into the editor first. Terminals and file panes both focus correctly on the same paths.

Found while removing bd_49Agents-7b2.7, the dead setupNoteEditorListeners that queried the same non-existent element. The dead branches were removed there; this is the behaviour they were masking.

The fix is small — noteEditors.get(id)?.monacoEditor?.focus(), which pane-creation.js already does when a note is first created — but it is a real behaviour change, not a cleanup. Focusing Monaco on every pane focus means it starts capturing keystrokes, which interacts with the Tab chords, so it wants a deliberate decision rather than being folded into a deletion.
title: A note pane never takes editor focus

acceptance_criteria: The updater refuses to install a tarball whose contents do not match a published checksum or signature. The reference value is produced by the build rather than maintained by hand. A tampered tarball fails with a clear error and leaves the existing install untouched.
description:
agent/src/updater.js downloads 49-agent.tar.gz, extracts it, checks only that agent/package.json exists inside, then renames it over the live install and exits so the supervisor restarts into it. There is no checksum and no signature at any point. The two comments that say 'verify integrity' and 'Verify the extracted content' describe a structure check, not an integrity one.

So anything that can serve or alter that tarball achieves arbitrary code execution as the agent user, persistently, on every machine that updates. That includes a compromised or misconfigured cloud server, and any network position able to tamper with the download.

PR #42 requires HTTPS for public hosts, which removes the in-transit case for those deployments. It does not help where the serving side is the problem, and plain HTTP remains permitted on private networks by necessity -- the installer emits ws:// for non-secure requests and start.sh suggests ws://192.168.1.10:1071, so LAN deployments cannot be required to use TLS.

Worth noting the tarball is also gitignored (cloud/dl/) and built by hand with 'tar czf cloud/dl/49-agent.tar.gz agent/', so today nothing records what a legitimate build should contain -- there is no reference to verify against even if the updater wanted to.

Options, roughly in order of effort: publish a SHA-256 alongside the tarball and have the updater compare before extracting; sign the tarball and ship the public key with the agent; or generate the checksum as part of the build so the reference is produced rather than maintained.
title: Agent updater installs the tarball with no integrity verification

close_reason: Already in main. Branch instance-isolation-bd_49Agents-ci3 has no unmerged commits, and src/config.js derives a per-port database path so a second instance cannot impersonate the first.
description:
Two 49Agents instances on different ports on the same machine stomp each other; only one agent connection works.

Root causes:
1. agent/bin/49-agent.js - PID file, cloud-url file, and token file are single global paths in ~/.49agents/. Second instance overwrites; stop kills wrong process.
2. agent/src/terminalManager.js - cleanupStalePorts() kills any process on 7700-7799 at startup, including the other instance's live ttyd terminals.
3. cloud/src/auth/agentAuth.js - dev token always resolves to constant agentId agent_dev_local, so agentHandler force-closes the other connection on same server.
4. cloud/src/config.js - dbPath defaults to ./data/tc.db regardless of PORT, so two servers share one SQLite DB and one local_auth identity row (CHECK id = 1).

Fix: derive an instance key from the cloud URL host:port (TC_INSTANCE overrides). Default port keeps the existing ~/.49agents/ layout; non-default ports get ~/.49agents/instances/<key>/. Partition the ttyd port range per instance. Persist a per-instance agent uuid. Derive cloud dbPath from PORT when DATABASE_PATH is unset. Pass PORT through from start.sh so keys line up.

Debugging-only capability (running several worktrees at once), not a user-facing feature.
title: Instance isolation: run multiple cloud+agent pairs on one machine for debugging

acceptance_criteria: Growing a terminal pane preserves its scrollback, without a manual window reload. A pane in the alternate screen is not reattached. Detection cannot loop on its own re-injection. The decision is a pure function with unit coverage.
description:
Making a terminal pane taller permanently loses scrollback. The workaround in use is reloading the whole window.

Mechanism, from our own code. xterm's baseY is the count of lines that have scrolled off into scrollback. When rows increases, xterm needs more visible rows and promotes lines out of scrollback into the viewport, so baseY falls. tmux knows nothing about xterm's scrollback: on resize it repaints its whole rows x cols pane with current content, and that repaint lands on the rows xterm just promoted. Those lines are gone. Shrinking a pane does not do this, which is why the loss is intermittent rather than constant.

safeFit (src-client/modules/editors.js:684) is a bare fitAddon.fit() behind a re-entrancy guard. Nothing tracks baseY and nothing restores scrollback.

The machinery for a fix already exists: reattachTerminal (modules/terminal-lifecycle.js:42) clears the buffer, resets _historyLoaded and _initialAttachDone, and re-attaches so the agent re-captures history, and app.js handles the re-injection. So the fix is to notice the drop and re-pull, which is what a manual reload already does by hand, scoped to one pane.

Two hazards to design around. Re-injection writes rows worth of newlines to push history into scrollback, which itself changes baseY, so a naive detector will loop. And the agent skips history capture while a pane is in the alternate screen, so reattaching a TUI would clear the buffer and get nothing back.

Provenance: this was reported in GitHub PR #11 by kr1json, which cannot be merged because the contributor has not signed the CLA. The approach there was the same -- detect the baseY drop, debounce, reattach -- and this issue exists to implement it independently. Prior work on adjacent history-loss bugs sits unmerged on the local fix-history-loss branch.
title: Terminal scrollback is destroyed when a pane grows taller

title: View mode toggle: prefs, hotkey, and on-screen control

acceptance_criteria: A page load with no file, note, or git-graph pane does not fetch Monaco, marked, DOMPurify, or the git-graph module. Opening each pane type still works, with a loading state while its dependency resolves. npm run build produces the required chunks.
close_reason:
Closed at the reduced scope, per user decision.

Delivered: Monaco, marked and DOMPurify are no longer declared in index.html and are fetched on first use by modules/lazy-deps.js -- well over a megabyte off every page load, for panes most sessions never open. e2e/lazy-deps.spec.js asserts a plain canvas load and list view fetch neither, that opening a note is what pulls the editor in, and that a second editor reuses the first fetch.

Doing this also surfaced and fixed the reason note markdown preview had never rendered (tracked and closed as bd_49Agents-jt4.15).

Not delivered: splitting the git-graph module out of the app bundle. Roughly 20K of a 577K bundle, and genuine splitting needs esbuild splitting:true plus outdir in build.js with terser and the obfuscator run over each emitted chunk. Carried forward as bd_49Agents-jt4.16 rather than dropped.
description:
public/index.html loads the Monaco AMD loader, marked, and DOMPurify from CDNs on every page load, and Monaco core is eagerly required into window.monacoReady. On a phone over cellular this is a large download for panes the user may never open. Convert these and the git-graph module to dynamic imports resolved on first use, adding the necessary entry points to cloud/build.js.

Touches desktop load paths, so this should land after the mobile-facing work.

acceptance_criteria: npm run test:e2e runs Playwright against the app under iPhone and Pixel emulation and covers pinch/pan, view mode toggling, and soft-keyboard viewport behaviour. npm test is unchanged and still fast.
close_reason:
Done. playwright.config.js runs iPhone 13 and Pixel 5 device projects on its own port, with a per-port database so a run never touches real data. npm run test:e2e is separate from npm test, which stays fast. 88 specs across boot, gestures, placement, view mode, lazy deps and the older mobile affordances.

Multi-touch is driven over CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent, since page.touchscreen only taps and a tap cannot express two fingers moving independently. Panes are seeded through the existing window.TC2_DEBUG rather than the add-pane flow, which cannot complete without a connected agent; no production hook was added.

Two traps the fixture has to defuse, both of which produce false passes rather than failures: a first-time visitor is redirected to /tutorial, whose tour renders its own #canvas and #zoom-in, and the first-run hotkey card is a bottom-centre overlay outside #canvas-container that swallows touches aimed at the lower half of the screen.

Not covered: WebKit. Agreed as Chromium-only, so iOS-specific behaviour -- the gesturestart guard, and soft-keyboard and safe-area handling -- still needs one pass on real hardware.
description:
There is no browser test harness; cloud/package.json runs node --test over test/*.test.js only. Mobile UI regressions are currently invisible. Add Playwright with iPhone and Pixel device descriptors, covering touch gestures, view mode switching, and the keyboard/viewport behaviour.

Keep it on a separate npm run test:e2e script so npm test stays fast.
title: Playwright test harness with mobile device emulation

acceptance_criteria: The card either does not appear on touch devices, or presents a mobile-appropriate equivalent that can be completed and dismissed by touch. Canvas gestures are not blocked by it while it is visible.
description:
The first-run hotkey card (_hotkeyTip, src-client/app.js:261) teaches Tab+H and Tab+M. On a phone there is no Tab key, so the card advertises two shortcuts the user cannot perform, and its self-clearing mechanism (press either hotkey) is unreachable. The only way out is the Got it button.

It is also positioned fixed at bottom-centre with min-width 300px and z-index 10050 (public/styles.css:7512), outside #canvas-container. Canvas touch listeners are attached to that container, so every touch landing on the card is invisible to them: on a 390px-wide viewport the card swallows gestures aimed at the lower-middle of the screen until it is dismissed.

Found while building the mobile e2e harness, which has to seed tc_hotkey_tip in localStorage to stop the card eating its touch input.
title: First-run hotkey card is unusable and blocks gestures on mobile

acceptance_criteria: Tapping the canvas in placement mode creates the pane at the tapped position on a touch device, with a sensible position when no hover has occurred. Covered by an e2e spec under device emulation that drives the real add-pane flow.
close_reason:
Closing as invalid -- this was my misdiagnosis, not a real defect. Placement does work on touch: a tap delivers a click to #canvas-container (the browser synthesises mousemove then click), handlePlacementClick runs, and it already falls back to reading the tap position directly when no hover has set a snapped one. The probe that suggested otherwise failed for an unrelated reason: every pane type is created through agentRequest, and no agent was connected under test.

Pinned anyway by e2e/placement.spec.js, since it is one preventDefault away from breaking -- handleTouchStart suppresses the default action on single-finger canvas touches and bails out during a placement specifically so the synthesised click survives.
description:
Creating any pane enters placement mode (src-client/modules/placement.js:58), which positions the ghost from mousemove and commits on a canvas-container click. A touch device produces neither: there is no mousemove before the tap, so snappedX/snappedY are never set, and the tap does not arrive as the click the handler expects.

The practical effect is that the add-pane menu opens and the ghost appears, but no pane can be created by touch. Confirmed under Playwright device emulation, where the add -> note -> tap-canvas sequence leaves state.panes empty; the e2e suite has to seed panes through window.TC2_DEBUG as a result.

This makes it the most severe mobile gap found so far: the app cannot be used to create anything on a phone.
design:
CORRECTION: this issue is invalid as filed and should be closed.

The original diagnosis blamed touch for the failure. Re-testing under device emulation shows the placement path does work on touch: a tap on the canvas in placement mode delivers a click to #canvas-container (Chromium synthesises mousemove then click from the tap), handlePlacementClick runs, the ghost is removed and createFn is called. handlePlacementClick also has a fallback for the no-hover case, computing the position straight from e.clientX/e.clientY, so it does not depend on a prior mousemove having set snappedX/snappedY.

The real reason no pane appeared in the probe is that every pane type is created through agentRequest -- createNotePane posts to /api/notes (src-client/modules/pane-creation.js:993) -- and the e2e environment has no agent connected over the WebSocket. Nothing to do with touch or mobile.

The e2e suite still seeds panes through window.TC2_DEBUG, but for that reason rather than the one originally recorded.
title: Placement mode cannot complete on a touch device

acceptance_criteria: A note's text-only toggle renders real markdown (headings, bold). With the sanitiser blocked, the preview shows escaped source and emits no live elements.
close_reason:
Fixed. loadMarkdown hides window.define while each UMD bundle evaluates so marked and DOMPurify take their browser-global branch instead of registering as anonymous AMD modules against Monaco's loader, and waits for any in-flight Monaco load first so it cannot pull define out from under Monaco's own module loader. It resolves only with both libraries in hand, closing the path that returned unsanitised HTML when DOMPurify was missing.

Covered by e2e/lazy-deps.spec.js: a note's text-only toggle now renders real markdown, and with the sanitiser blocked the preview shows escaped source and emits no live elements.
description:
marked and DOMPurify are UMD bundles whose first branch is typeof define === 'function' && define.amd. Monaco's AMD loader defines exactly that, and public/index.html loaded Monaco's loader.min.js before both libraries, so each registered as an anonymous AMD module and neither window.marked nor window.DOMPurify was ever assigned. renderMarkdownPreview guarded on if (window.marked), so the guard was permanently false and every note preview silently fell back to escaped plain text with newlines converted to
. The text-only toggle on a note has therefore never rendered markdown. The same code path had a second problem: when marked was present but DOMPurify was not, it returned marked's unsanitised output (window.DOMPurify ? sanitize(raw) : raw), making note content an XSS vector. Both fixed in modules/lazy-deps.js: loadMarkdown hides window.define while each UMD bundle evaluates so it takes the browser-global branch, waits for any in-flight Monaco load first so it cannot pull define out from under Monaco's module loader, and resolves only with both libraries in hand so there is no unsanitised path. Covered by e2e/lazy-deps.spec.js.
title: Note markdown preview never rendered: UMD libraries lost to Monaco's AMD loader

acceptance_criteria: A page load with no git-graph, beads, folder or conversations pane does not download those modules. Opening each still works, with a loading state while its chunk resolves. npm run build emits and obfuscates every chunk, and the app boots from public/ with no unresolved imports. e2e coverage asserts the chunks are absent on a plain load.
description:
Carried forward from bd_49Agents-jt4.11, which delivered on-demand loading for the three CDN libraries but left the app bundle itself whole.

cloud/build.js bundles src-client/app.js into a single file with esbuild, then runs terser and javascript-obfuscator over it and writes one public/app.min.js. Modules for panes a session never opens are therefore always downloaded: git-graph, beads, folder, conversations, and the git-graph renderer are the obvious candidates.

Scope is small in payload terms and non-trivial in build terms, which is why it was deferred: git-graph alone is roughly 20K of a 577K bundle. Real splitting needs esbuild splitting:true with outdir instead of write:false, then terser and the obfuscator applied to each emitted chunk with the inter-chunk import specifiers surviving obfuscation and still resolving from public/. Worth doing only if bundle size becomes a real concern -- the megabyte that dominated first load has already gone.
title: Split the app bundle so pane modules load on demand

close_reason: Implemented and now verified. The bottom sheet lists every pane with type icon, label, device badge and shortcut number, and tapping one jumps to the pane and expands it -- all covered in e2e/mobile-basics.spec.js. Also fixed: the button was only created when the page loaded below 768px, so rotating a tablet into portrait or dragging a window narrow left no way to reach the drawer without a reload. The stylesheet already governs its visibility, so the gate only removed the element the CSS was there to manage.
description: No way to see or jump to panes on mobile without zooming out. Add a swipe-up drawer or bottom sheet listing all panes with tap-to-jump. Should show pane type icon, name/title, device badge, and shortcut number. Tapping jumps to pane and auto-expands it.
title: Mobile pane list / navigation drawer

close_reason:
All three measures are in place: user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1.0 in the viewport meta (plus viewport-fit=cover, added for safe-area insets), touch-action: none on html/body, and gesturestart/gesturechange preventDefault in setupEventListeners. Covered in e2e/mobile-basics.spec.js by asserting the meta contents, the computed touch-action, and behaviourally that a canvas pan does not scroll the document.

Caveat: gesturestart/gesturechange are WebKit-only events, so that specific guard cannot be exercised under the Chromium-based e2e suite. It needs one pass on a real iOS device to be certain.
description: Safari's built-in pinch-to-zoom can fire alongside our canvas pinch handler, causing double-zoom or page zoom on top of canvas zoom. Need to add a viewport meta tag with user-scalable=no and handle touch-action CSS properly. Also add gesturestart/gesturechange preventDefault for Safari-specific gesture events.
title: Prevent Safari native pinch-to-zoom conflict

close_reason:
This was genuinely broken, not merely untested. The client did detect a coarse pointer and prefer click focus (app.js:1226), but the branch was dead: the route answered prefs.focus_mode || 'hover', which is always truthy, so the client always took the stored-preference path and every touch device kept hover focus -- where focus fires on each tap.

Fixed by making 'never chosen' representable end to end: DEFAULTS.focus_mode is null and the route passes an absent value through instead of defaulting it. A stored choice still wins, so anyone who picked hover on a tablet keeps it, and the column keeps its hover default for existing rows. Covered by test/focus-mode-default.test.js.
description: Focus mode defaults to 'hover' which causes accidental pane focus on touch devices (touchstart triggers hover-like behavior). Should auto-detect touch-primary devices and default to 'click' focus mode. Use (pointer: coarse) media query or ontouchstart detection at init time.
title: Auto-enable click focus mode on touch devices

close_reason:
Implemented and now verified. autoArrangePanes stacks every pane into a single column sized to the viewport width, ordered by shortcut number, and resets the view to the top; it is reachable from the Arrange button in the nav drawer. Covered in e2e/mobile-basics.spec.js, which asserts a shared left edge and width, no overlap between consecutive panes, a width matched to the viewport, and the view reset.

Not done, and deliberately: the description's optional 'trigger automatically on first load below 768px'. Rearranging a user's canvas without being asked destroys deliberate layout, and list view now covers the same need without moving anything.
description: On small screens, panes positioned for desktop end up scattered and hard to find. Add an auto-arrange option that stacks panes vertically in a single column, sized to viewport width minus margins. Could trigger automatically on first load if viewport < 768px, or offer a button in the mobile nav drawer.
title: Auto-layout / snap-to-grid for mobile viewports

close_reason:
Implemented and now verified. The touchend handler in pane-interaction.js carries no type guard and expands any pane on a tap below 768px, within the dx/dy < 15px and 400ms thresholds. Covered in e2e/mobile-basics.spec.js: a tap on a note pane expands it, and a drag across the same pane does not.

Worth recording from writing that spec: a pane at the canvas origin sits behind the HUD and cannot be tapped at all, so the spec places it mid-screen.
description: Currently only terminal panes auto-expand on tap (<768px). File, note, beads, folder, git-graph, and iframe panes should also auto-expand on tap since they're too small to interact with on a phone screen without expanding. The tap detection logic (dx<15, dy<15, elapsed<400ms) already exists -- just remove the type===terminal guard.
title: Extend auto-expand tap to all pane types on mobile

acceptance_criteria: Pinch starts from a finger on a pane; pinch pans and zooms together; lifting one finger degrades to a single-finger pan without freezing; touchcancel resets state and removes listeners; a fit-to-content control exists; soft keyboard does not cover the terminal prompt; fixed controls respect safe-area insets. Pure gesture math lives in a testable module with node --test coverage.
close_reason:
Done. modules/gestures.js holds the pan and zoom arithmetic as pure functions over an immutable view, covered by 26 unit tests, and handleTouchStart is rebuilt on top of it. All seven defects addressed: pinch now starts over a pane (capture-phase registration, since pane content stopPropagations touchstart), a pinch pans as well as scales, finger-count changes re-anchor in either direction instead of freezing, touchcancel ends the session rather than leaking a listener per gesture, every commit is clamped so a fling cannot strand the viewport, momentum reads event timeStamp, and setZoom shares one clamp with the touch path.

The root cause underneath all of it: _ctx.canvasContainer never existed on that context -- only getCanvasContainer() -- so the old handler threw a TypeError on the first touchstart and canvas touch pan and pinch had never worked at all. Restoring the bad reference fails five gesture specs.

visualViewport tracking and env() safe-area insets are in modules/viewport.js, with the fixed controls, nav sheet and expanded pane measuring their gaps from the safe area. Covered by e2e/gestures.spec.js and e2e/boot.spec.js.
description:
handleTouchStart (src-client/modules/canvas-events.js:220) has seven concrete defects that make canvas navigation on a phone unreliable:

1. The e.target gate at line 221 only starts a gesture when the finger lands exactly on the canvas or its container. On a phone, panes cover most of the screen, so most pinch attempts silently do nothing.
2. Pinch cannot pan. Two-finger handling applies scale around the midpoint but never applies midpoint movement to panX/panY.
3. Lifting one finger from a pinch kills the gesture. touchend tears down both handlers even with a finger still down, and startX/startY are never recomputed, so pinch-to-drag freezes the canvas.
4. No touchcancel listener. An interrupted gesture (call, notification, system swipe) leaves isPanning true and leaks a touchmove listener per gesture.
5. No pan bounds. Momentum can fling the viewport into empty space, and the 0.05 minimum zoom makes 'zoom out to find things' illegible.
6. No visualViewport handling. The soft keyboard covers the terminal prompt and xterm rows are never recomputed.
7. No env(safe-area-inset-*) anywhere in styles.css, so fixed controls sit under the notch and home bar.
title: Fix touch pan/pinch gesture bugs on canvas

acceptance_criteria: A control frames all panes in the viewport from any pan/zoom state. Bounding-box and zoom math is a pure function with node --test coverage.
close_reason: Done. zoom-fit frames the whole content box against the safe-area-inset viewport, and the existing zoom buttons now anchor on that same rect rather than the raw window, so repeated presses on a device with a cutout no longer walk the view sideways. fitToBounds is a pure function with unit coverage including the single-small-pane and zero-area cases; e2e/gestures.spec.js drives it from a viewport parked far away at 0.06 zoom and asserts both extremes of the content box land on screen.
description: The canvas has no escape hatch when the viewport is panned away from all panes. Zooming out to find them bottoms out at 0.05, where nothing is legible. Add a control that computes the bounding box of all panes and sets zoom and pan to frame it within the viewport, respecting safe-area insets.
title: Add a fit-to-content / zoom-to-fit canvas control

acceptance_criteria: Toggling to list mode replaces the canvas with a scrollable pane list; tapping an entry opens that pane. The bottom sheet still works in canvas mode. Label/icon logic is shared between the two, not duplicated.
close_reason:
Done. modules/view-mode.js renders a persistent list that replaces the canvas, ordered by shortcut number then reading order, carrying each pane's device and Claude state -- rows needing a human pulse, working and idle stay quiet. The state is read from the classes the canvas already puts on pane elements, so there is no second source of truth.

The bottom sheet stays as the quick peek, as agreed. Labelling and ordering moved to modules/pane-summary.js, shared by both so they cannot disagree about what a pane is called; its fallbacks are unit-tested, including the malformed-url case that would otherwise throw out of new URL().

Two consequences of hiding the canvas rather than covering it, both handled: switching collapses an expanded pane (it is reparented to body and would float over the list), and starting a new pane returns to the canvas first, since placement puts a ghost there. Covered by e2e/view-mode.spec.js.
description:
A persistent view mode that replaces the canvas with a scrollable list of panes, for viewports where pan/zoom navigation is impractical. The existing bottom sheet (setupMobileNavDrawer, src-client/modules/menus.js:207) stays as the quick-peek gesture while in canvas mode; list mode is the sustained-use view.

Pane label and icon logic currently inline in menus.js:229-249 should be factored out and shared rather than duplicated.
title: List view mode as an alternative to the canvas

close_reason: Already in main. cloud/src-client/ has 32 modules and app.js imports them; branch split-app-modules-k0v has no unmerged commits. Never closed at the time.

close_reason: Already in main. The pulsing .add-machine-fleet-btn is implemented in modules/agent-ui.js.

close_reason: Closing as obsolete rather than done. Guest mode was deliberately removed rather than built: commit 63390a8 'Remove OAuth and guest mode from cloud-hosted deployment'. The issue describes a product direction that was reversed.

acceptance_criteria: Scrolling in a pane attached to an external tmux session no longer injects arrow keys and no longer alters the command line. Arrow-key scrolling still works for genuine alternate-screen TUIs such as vim and htop. The scroll-path decision is a pure function with unit coverage.
close_reason:
Fixed; PR #59 is open and awaiting review, rebased clean onto main with cla passing.

The issue's suspected cause was obsolete — the browser no longer sends terminal:scroll anywhere, so the copy-mode leak it blames cannot happen. Verified the real cause against tmux 3.6a on an isolated server: an attached inner tmux reports alternate_on=1 and pane_current_command=tmux, and the wheel handler read alternate screen as 'a TUI that scrolls with arrows' and sent Up/Down into the pane, where the inner tmux's readline treated Up as previous-command. The damage was to input, not just to scrolling.

The proposed signal was right but unavailable: the agent sent the foreground command only for Claude panes. Now carried for all, with a test pinning both ends of that wire.
description:
GitHub issue #20 (EugeneChan00): scrolling in a pane that has attached to an external tmux session cycles previous commands instead of scrolling history.

The issue's suspected cause is obsolete. It blames the hybrid scroll sending terminal:scroll, the agent entering tmux copy-mode on the outer session, and those keystrokes leaking into the attached inner session as Up arrow. The client no longer sends terminal:scroll anywhere -- the message constant (agent/src/protocol.js:20), the router case (messageRouter.js:237) and terminalManager.scrollTerminal with its copy-mode calls (tmux.js:536) are all still present but unreachable from the browser.

The real path produces the identical symptom by a different route:
- An attached inner tmux puts the outer pane into the alternate screen. Verified directly on an isolated tmux server: with a client attached inside the pane, the outer pane reports alternate_on=1 and pane_current_command=tmux.
- The agent polls #{alternate_on} and reports alternateOn (tmux.js:596).
- The client stores it as termInfo._alternateOn (claude-states.js:68).
- The wheel handler treats alternate screen as 'a TUI app that scrolls with arrows' and sends \x1b[A / \x1b[B into the pane (editors.js:740-748).
- The inner tmux forwards those to its active pane's shell, where readline reads Up as previous-command.

So the issue's proposed detection signal (pane_current_command === 'tmux') is right, but it is not currently available to the client: the agent drops command from the states payload for non-Claude terminals (tmux.js:756, and the default at :719), sending it only for Claude panes.

Note on the remedy: falling back to xterm.scrollLines() as the issue suggests stops the corruption but will not actually scroll, because in the alternate screen there is no meaningful scrollback in xterm's alternate buffer. Scrolling a nested tmux properly requires the inner tmux's own mechanism. Where the inner tmux has mouse mode on, areMouseEventsActive is already true and the existing mouse re-dispatch path handles it correctly, so this fix only changes the mouse-off case -- from actively corrupting the command line to doing nothing.
title: Scroll sends arrow keys into an attached tmux, cycling command history

close_reason: Already in main. desktop/ is present and branch electron-desktop-bd_49Agents-y09 has no unmerged commits.

Electron main process spawns the cloud server and agent as child processes, finds a free port, and tears everything down on quit. Includes electron-builder config for eventual .dmg distribution. Startup check for tmux and ttyd with graceful error if missing.
title: Electron desktop app wrapper for macOS
